mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth, as indicated by GDPC1, suggests a robust economy, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of 60-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity, which can lead to higher equity prices as companies increase output and revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of 60-day windows, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) slows and unemployment (UNRATE) rises simultaneously, it indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 slows and UNRATE rises but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of 20-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4% indicates tighter monetary policy, which can lead to decreased liquidity and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of 5-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing real sales (RSAFS) growth indicates weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth slows but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of 60-day windows, the hypothesis is falsified.
